citation: Alonso and Andrews, Can city deals improve economic performance?
comparator: Eligible non-participating local governments and timing contrasts
outcomes: Real GDP growth, GVA growth, job-density growth
key_findings: Overall positive associations; roughly 2.5-3% gains concentrated in Wave 1; no clear Wave 2 gains
limitations: Deals bundled funding and governance; Wave 1 had stronger prior institutions; funding details incomplete
quality_rationale: Modern staggered DiD and robustness checks, but selection, bundled treatments and unobserved institutional histories constrain attribution
transferability_notes: Direct English institutional and fiscal context
portfolio_tags: Transport; housing; skills; business; culture; digital
decision_relevance: Supports staged devolution and prior capability investment, not uniform effects
verification_status: Opened full-text PDF; DOI/publication details checked

citation: Arends, The Dangers of Fiscal Decentralization and Public Service Delivery
comparator: Arguments and evidence for centralised and decentralised delivery
key_findings: Evidence supports both proponents and sceptics; effects vary by service, design and context
limitations: Not a systematic meta-analysis and mostly indirect to England
quality_rationale: Balanced design-aware review but no pooled causal estimate
transferability_notes: Mechanisms transfer; constitutional and service systems vary
decision_relevance: Requires service-specific rather than blanket presumption

citation: Baskaran, Feld and Schnellenbach, Fiscal Federalism, Decentralization, and Economic Growth
key_findings: Median estimate not statistically significant; results sensitive to how autonomy and models are measured
limitations: Underlying studies heterogeneous and often use poor autonomy proxies
quality_rationale: Formal meta-analysis directly addresses heterogeneous empirical estimates and publication/model characteristics
transferability_notes: OECD evidence relevant; English powers and fiscal autonomy are narrower than many systems
decision_relevance: Rejects an automatic aggregate growth dividend
verification_status: Publisher abstract and full working version checked

citation: Baxter et al., The effects of integrated care
design: Systematic review with comparative strength rating
key_findings: Evidence favoured perceived quality, satisfaction and access; other system and cost outcomes limited or inconsistent
direction: Supportive for access; null/mixed for costs
limitations: Heterogeneous models and designs; limited service-user outcomes; causal attribution difficult
quality_rationale: Registered systematic review with transparent synthesis across a large evidence base
transferability_notes: Developed-country services include UK; exact governance and funding arrangements vary
decision_relevance: Supports outcome claims more than savings claims
verification_status: PubMed and open full text checked

citation: BEIS/Warwick, Evaluation of Devolved Institutions
design: Qualitative interviews, case studies and document review
intervention_or_exposure: Creation and development of devolved institutions
key_findings: Arrangements were fragmented and asymmetric; setup was burdensome; systematic external engagement was limited; capability and cultural support needed
limitations: Designed mainly for process and theory development; cannot estimate outcome effects
quality_rationale: Direct and well-documented process evaluation, but not an impact evaluation
transferability_notes: Direct English institutions
decision_relevance: Shows capability and civic engagement must be built into transition

citation: Bevan and Hood, What's measured is what matters
design: Analytical case study using English NHS performance evidence
key_findings: Narrow high-stakes targets produced measurement and gaming problems; audit and target design require safeguards
limitations: Observational and historical; cannot quantify net effect of targets
quality_rationale: Direct, influential empirical case analysis but no counterfactual causal design
transferability_notes: Direct English performance-management setting
decision_relevance: Warns against single high-stakes indicators
verification_status: Publisher and archived full text checked

citation: Björkman and Svensson, Power to the People
population_or_system: 50 communities in nine districts using primary health centres
intervention_or_exposure: Facilitated community monitoring and action plans
outcomes: Utilisation, provider behaviour, service quality, under-five mortality
key_findings: Utilisation and provider behaviour improved; under-five mortality fell 33% with a wide 90% CI of 8-64%
limitations: Small number of clusters; rural low-income setting; intensive facilitation
quality_rationale: Randomised design and multiple measured outcomes, with uncertainty reported
transferability_notes: Supports accountability mechanism, not direct institutional transfer to England
decision_relevance: Shows information plus organised capacity and consequences can work

citation: Brachert, Dettmann and Titze, The regional effects of a place-based policy
key_findings: Positive GVA and productivity growth; no employment or gross-wage effect
limitations: Evaluates grants, not devolution; local spillovers and longer-run distribution remain uncertain
quality_rationale: Credible discontinuity design with multiple economic outcomes
transferability_notes: Comparable developed system, but programme and fiscal framework differ
decision_relevance: Shows outcome dimensions can diverge even under effective place investment

citation: Britteon et al., The effect of devolution on health
key_findings: Life expectancy increased by 0.196 years; larger gains for men and deprived/low-baseline areas
limitations: Single mature region; bundled reform and co-interventions; synthetic-control assumptions
quality_rationale: Strong direct quasi-experimental design with transparent comparator and uncertainty
transferability_notes: Direct England but generalisation from GM is limited
decision_relevance: Best direct evidence for positive population-health effects

citation: Britteon et al., The impact of devolution on local health systems
design: Generalised synthetic control with multiple-testing adjustment and document analysis
population_or_system: Local health system; 98 indicators to February 2020
intervention_or_exposure: Health and social-care devolution and aligned reforms
comparator: Synthetic control from other English areas
outcomes: System functions, intermediate objectives, final health goals, social determinants
key_findings: Life expectancy and healthy life expectancy increased; improvements across several service and social-determinant domains; outpatient, mental-health, maternity and dental results mixed
limitations: Single region; bundled transformation funding and relationships; 98 outcomes; some attribution uncertainty
quality_rationale: Broad direct outcome set, synthetic control and multiple-testing adjustment
transferability_notes: Direct but GM maturity, resources and relationships constrain transfer
portfolio_tags: Health; social care; transport; housing; employment
decision_relevance: Supports alignment mechanisms while showing mixed service effects
verification_status: University record and DOI abstract checked

citation: Channa and Faguet, Decentralization of Health and Education
key_findings: Unweighted evidence weak and contradictory; higher-quality evidence more positive for technical efficiency and education preference matching; prerequisites under-researched
limitations: Developing-country settings; heterogeneity; mechanisms poorly measured
quality_rationale: Explicit quality adjustment changes inference and addresses study design
transferability_notes: Mechanisms transfer, system conditions do not directly
decision_relevance: Supports conditional rather than universal service claims

citation: Charbit, From de jure to de facto decentralised public policies
key_findings: Contracts can improve information and coordination and reduce transaction costs but have drawbacks; mutual dependence remains
limitations: Primarily conceptual and case-based; outcome causality not established
quality_rationale: Relevant synthesis of mechanisms but limited comparative causal evidence
transferability_notes: Directly relevant to multi-level governance; contract design varies
decision_relevance: Supports negotiated interfaces rather than central withdrawal

citation: Ferraz and Finan, Exposing Corrupt Politicians
design: Random timing of municipal audits before/after election
key_findings: Average effect was not significant; effects varied with disclosed corruption: three violations reduced re-election by 17.7 percentage points; local radio strengthened effects
limitations: Electoral and media setting differs; outcome is sanction rather than service performance
quality_rationale: Quasi-random disclosure timing supports causal inference and heterogeneity analysis
transferability_notes: Mechanism transfers if information is legible and media/sanctions exist
decision_relevance: Shows transparency needs content, transmission and consequences

citation: Gemmell, Kneller and Sanz, Fiscal Decentralization and Economic Growth
key_findings: Spending decentralisation associated with lower growth; revenue decentralisation with higher growth; matching responsibilities matters
limitations: Non-experimental cross-country panel; autonomy measurement and endogeneity concerns
quality_rationale: Sophisticated panel method and separates revenue/spending, but residual confounding remains
transferability_notes: OECD systems relevant; assignment and autonomy differ materially
decision_relevance: Supports aligned revenue and spending rather than expenditure devolution alone

citation: IFS, The short- and medium-term effects of Sure Start
source_type: Research institute impact evaluation and cost-benefit synthesis
design: Difference-in-differences using phased rollout and linked administrative data
comparator: Earlier cohorts and comparison areas before/after openings
outcomes: Health, education, SEND, social care, offending, earnings and fiscal benefits
key_findings: Long-lasting benefits; central estimate total long-run financial benefits about twice upfront cost; public-purse benefits alone slightly below full cost
limitations: Programme was centrally funded and locally delivered, not a test of devolution; some lifetime benefits projected
quality_rationale: Large administrative datasets, longitudinal outcomes and quasi-experimental rollout design
transferability: High for prevention; Low for devolution
transferability_notes: Direct England programme evidence but governance mechanism differs
portfolio_tags: Children; youth; families; health; education; civil society
decision_relevance: Strong evidence that selected prevention can pay off; no automatic fiscal-devolution inference
verification_status: IFS report and methods pages checked

citation: IFS, Reforming local government funding in England
key_findings: Equalisation reduces capacity disparities; resets and formulas can create gaming and incentive trade-offs; outcome evidence on decentralisation remains weak
limitations: Policy modelling/review rather than programme impact evaluation
quality_rationale: Detailed direct fiscal-system analysis with transparent institutional trade-offs
transferability_notes: Direct England finance context
decision_relevance: Treats equalisation as core architecture

citation: IFS, Government plans for tax revenue sharing with England's mayors: response
design: Ex ante fiscal incidence and risk analysis
intervention_or_exposure: Assignment of a share of income-tax revenues
comparator: Current grant-based arrangements and design variants
key_findings: Could strengthen growth incentives and certainty; risks arise from shocks beyond mayoral control, volatility and unequal tax bases; equalisation design is decisive
limitations: Ex ante and not an evaluation; final design not settled
quality_rationale: Expert direct analysis of current proposal but prospective
transferability_notes: Direct proposed English system
decision_relevance: Requires shock insurance and explicit reset/equalisation rules
verification_status: Permanent IFS article opened and checked

citation: Jong et al., Urban productivity effects of local governments
intervention_or_exposure: Local autonomy, government quality and fragmentation
key_findings: Productivity lower on average in more decentralised countries; positive relation under high government quality and low fragmentation; highest with autonomy, quality and low fragmentation
limitations: Observational; governance measures may be endogenous; city composition differs
quality_rationale: Large comparative panel explicitly models interacting institutional conditions
transferability_notes: European urban systems relevant; English local autonomy remains distinctive
decision_relevance: Makes institutional quality and boundary design causal conditions

citation: Mansuri and Rao, Localizing Development: Does Participation Work?
outcomes: Participation, capture, service and welfare outcomes
key_findings: Effects depend on context, state capacity, facilitation and learning; elite capture and collective-action constraints are common; M&E often weak
limitations: Wide heterogeneity and much evidence from lower-income settings
quality_rationale: Comprehensive critical synthesis attentive to design and context
transferability_notes: Mechanisms transfer; political and administrative settings vary
decision_relevance: Participation must be designed and supported

citation: Masters et al., Return on investment of public health interventions
key_findings: Median reported ROI 14.3; local interventions 4.1 and national programmes 27.2; wide range and intervention heterogeneity
limitations: Variable study quality, inconsistent valuation, expected publication bias; medians not pooled causal effects
quality_rationale: Systematic identification and transparent caveats, but economic methods and interventions highly heterogeneous
transferability: Medium-High for prevention; Low for devolution
transferability_notes: High-income universal-care settings relevant; programme mix differs
decision_relevance: Supports prevention potential but not universal savings or local superiority

citation: Moss et al., Impact of Devolution on Local Health System Financing
key_findings: Total annual spending rose about £66.58 per capita and local public health/social care about £36.39; several component categories had no significant change
limitations: Single region; finance flows do not establish efficiency; reform and funding bundled
quality_rationale: Direct quasi-experimental finance analysis with explicit confidence intervals
transferability_notes: Direct England but GM maturity and specific funding matter
decision_relevance: Outcome gains were not evidence of immediate spending reduction
verification_status: Full text and journal metadata checked

citation: National Audit Office, Whole-Place Community Budgets
design: Review of 181 publications and pilot business cases
population_or_system: Four Whole Place Community Budget pilots and prior integration literature
intervention_or_exposure: Local cross-service integration and pooled/aligned resources
outcomes: Service outcomes, costs and projected benefits
key_findings: Limited evidence that joint working/resource alignment improved impact; business-case approach promising but projected benefits depended on assumptions
limitations: Pilots early; benefit estimates prospective and context-specific
quality_rationale: Independent audit directly tests evidence and assumptions rather than accepting business cases
transferability_notes: Direct English local-service integration
decision_relevance: Requires robust counterfactuals and cashability tests

citation: National Audit Office, English devolution deals
key_findings: Government had not set clear measures to assess success; accountability and administrative/geographic complexity created risks
limitations: Early implementation; not an outcomes evaluation
quality_rationale: Independent direct audit of design and evaluability
transferability_notes: Direct English arrangements
decision_relevance: Establishes need for baseline outcomes and transparent responsibility

citation: National Audit Office, Central oversight of arm's-length bodies
population_or_system: ALBs spending £265bn and employing around 300,000 in 2018-19
intervention_or_exposure: Creation, classification and oversight of ALBs
key_findings: Arm's-length arrangements can protect expertise and independence; inconsistent setup and oversight limit learning and risk management
limitations: Does not evaluate localisation or reintegration of ALB functions
quality_rationale: Independent system-level audit with direct evidence on model selection and oversight
transferability: High for oversight; Low for transfer option
transferability_notes: UK central machinery directly relevant, but no place-transfer comparator
decision_relevance: Supports function tests, not blanket transfer

citation: National Audit Office, Introducing Integrated Care Systems
outcomes: Readiness, capacity, accountability, finance and workforce
key_findings: Potential benefits faced risks from national-local target tension, workforce, finance and social-care pressures; national strategies, time and relationships required
limitations: Early-stage review; not an impact or value-for-money conclusion
quality_rationale: Independent direct implementation evidence with system-wide scope
transferability_notes: Direct English integrated-service context
decision_relevance: Shows centre and place have complementary enabling roles

citation: National Audit Office, Devolution in England: funding and accountability
design: Audit of integrated settlements, reporting and accountability
population_or_system: Mayoral strategic authorities and central departments
outcomes: Flexibility, reporting burden, underperformance and capacity
key_findings: Settlements enabled longer-term thinking; reporting burden exceeded expectations; underperformance regime untested; local and central capacity and scrutiny need strengthening
limitations: Too early to establish outcomes or value for money
quality_rationale: Current independent evidence directly on implementation and accountability
transferability_notes: Direct current England reforms
decision_relevance: Supports simplification with stronger local accountability, not removal of assurance

citation: Neumark and Simpson, Place-Based Policies
design: Handbook review of theory and empirical evaluations
population_or_system: Enterprise zones, structural funds, clusters and local subsidies
outcomes: Employment, wages, output, property and distribution
key_findings: Enterprise-zone evidence mixed; some other tools positive; displacement, capitalisation, in-movers and landlord gains can alter incidence
limitations: Interventions and designs heterogeneous; not devolution evidence
quality_rationale: Authoritative comprehensive review distinguishes mechanisms and incidence
transferability_notes: Developed systems relevant but policy instruments differ
portfolio_tags: Business; creative clusters; visitor economy; housing
decision_relevance: Requires additionality and beneficiary/displacement analysis

citation: OECD, Making Decentralisation Work
key_findings: Outcomes depend on design; recommends clear responsibilities, adequate resources, capacity, coordination, accountability and experimentation
limitations: Predominantly synthesis and practice; limited direct causal estimation
quality_rationale: Broad authoritative comparative evidence with explicit design principles
transferability_notes: OECD contexts useful if autonomy, scale and equalisation are coded
decision_relevance: Core source for conditional architecture

citation: OECD, Effective Multi-level Public Investment
key_findings: Effective investment requires cross-level and cross-jurisdiction coordination, capability and framework conditions
limitations: Principles are mainly correlational/practice-based; no single causal effect size
quality_rationale: Systematic comparative implementation framework but non-experimental
transferability_notes: Public-investment institutions broadly comparable
decision_relevance: Supports functional geographies and shared capacity

citation: OECD, Synthesising good practices in fiscal federalism
design: OECD cross-country research and country-survey synthesis
intervention_or_exposure: Tax autonomy, assignments, equalisation and rules
outcomes: Services, efficiency, equity and fiscal stability
key_findings: Recommends matching own revenue and spending, clear responsibilities, equalisation, coordination, transparency, data and professional capacity; spending shares do not measure autonomy
limitations: Noncausal synthesis; national systems differ
quality_rationale: Authoritative direct fiscal-design synthesis with explicit caveats
transferability_notes: Comparable high-income settings, requiring constitutional coding
decision_relevance: Supports coherent fiscal package and rejects crude decentralisation metrics

citation: OECD, Regional Governance in OECD Countries
outcomes: Coordination, democracy, capacity and service scale
key_findings: Asymmetry is used to match capacity, pilot powers and recognise territorial needs; adequately funded/capable regions can coordinate at larger-than-municipal scale
limitations: Descriptive/comparative rather than causal
quality_rationale: Comprehensive official comparison, but claims rely largely on institutional practice
transferability_notes: Strong for design options; exact English legal autonomy differs
decision_relevance: Supports staged/asymmetric models with anti-divergence safeguards

citation: OECD, Place-Based Policies for the Future
design: Expert workshops and synthesis of systematic reviews
population_or_system: Nearly 15,000 local-development evaluations represented in cited reviews
key_findings: Only about 2% met minimum robustness; among robust studies about half positive and half limited; effects depend on targeting, coherence, scale, implementation and governance
limitations: Umbrella synthesis; robustness threshold and intervention mix vary; negative results may be under-detected
quality_rationale: Transparent authoritative synthesis, but not a new systematic review of primary studies
transferability_notes: Advanced-economy policy design broadly relevant
decision_relevance: Shows both promise and severe evaluation weakness

citation: Rodríguez-Pose and Ezcurra, Does decentralization matter for regional disparities?
comparator: Variation over time and between countries
key_findings: No overall association; effects contingent on development, baseline disparities and redistributive capacity; high-income countries showed, if anything, lower disparity
limitations: Small country panel; instrument and cross-country comparability concerns
quality_rationale: Directly tests disparities with IV but substantial institutional heterogeneity remains
transferability_notes: High-income subgroup relevant; English equalisation and autonomy distinctive
decision_relevance: Shows distribution cannot be inferred from decentralisation alone

citation: Rodríguez-Pose and Ezcurra, Is fiscal decentralization harmful for economic growth?
design: Cross-country growth regressions with fiscal, political and administrative measures
key_findings: Fiscal decentralisation negatively and significantly associated with growth across specifications; political/administrative effects weaker and measurement-sensitive
limitations: Observational cross-country design; decentralisation endogenous; short period and aggregate measures
quality_rationale: Robust specification checks but causal identification remains limited
transferability_notes: OECD relevance with important English institutional differences
decision_relevance: Strong counterweight to growth claims, not definitive causal proof

citation: Sapkota et al., The impact of decentralisation on health systems
design: Umbrella review across WHO building blocks
comparator: Centralised or alternative arrangements across reviews
outcomes: Governance, finance, workforce, information, medicines and service delivery
key_findings: Impacts were inconsistently reported; effects varied by building block, implementation and context
limitations: Small number and mixed quality of reviews; predominantly lower/middle-income settings
quality_rationale: Systematic umbrella design explicitly maps conflicting evidence and quality
transferability_notes: Mechanisms transfer; health financing and constitutional settings often do not
decision_relevance: Challenges universal health-system claims

citation: Stossberg, Bartolini and Blöchliger, Fiscal decentralisation and income inequality
population_or_system: National/subnational fiscal systems and household income distributions
key_findings: Small/unstable Gini reduction; more stable evidence that low-income groups diverged from median under some tax autonomy while upper-middle gaps narrowed
limitations: Observational panel; country comparability; outcome sensitive to measure
quality_rationale: Direct distributional analysis with multiple measures and robustness checks
transferability_notes: OECD settings relevant; tax mix and welfare systems differ
decision_relevance: Requires distributional analysis beyond headline averages

citation: Sweeney, Devolution and economic growth in England's City Regions
design: Difference-in-differences/fixed effects with matched and event-study robustness
outcomes: GDP/GVA per capita and within-MCA convergence
key_findings: Little evidence of overall growth acceleration; results largely null or negative; richer districts in some MCAs grew faster while poorer districts fell behind
limitations: Six-year follow-up; bundled policies; treatment timing and compositional differences; mayoral status may be incomplete proxy for powers
quality_rationale: Direct recent English panel with multiple robustness tests; nonrandom assignment remains
transferability_notes: Direct England setting
decision_relevance: Central evidence against general and inclusive growth claims

citation: Wilkoszewski and Sundby, Steering from the Centre
design: Conceptual analysis and three comparative cases
geography: Norway, Germany and EU education governance
intervention_or_exposure: Central steering through exchange, capacity and coordination
key_findings: Cases shared multi-stage processes, transparency/publicity and soft sanctions; centre retains information, capability and objective-setting roles
limitations: Three heterogeneous cases; outcome effectiveness not causally identified
quality_rationale: Useful mechanism cases but limited causal and sectoral breadth
transferability_notes: Advanced multi-level systems; education-specific
decision_relevance: Supports a different centre, not simple withdrawal

citation: World Bank/Ahmad et al., Decentralization and Service Delivery
key_findings: Institutional arrangements, incentives and capability determine whether decentralisation improves delivery; formal transfer alone is insufficient
limitations: Older framework; many developing-country examples; no pooled impact estimate
quality_rationale: Influential structured synthesis but limited causal identification
transferability_notes: Mechanisms transfer; fiscal and administrative systems differ
decision_relevance: Supports coherent authority-finance-accountability package
